code_contract_review: Selected UART DMA and RX-block modes test DMA1EN plus both DMA1RST and DMA2RST, consistent with both resets affecting shared DMAMUX1. Only those two selected state types add a sticky bool; ordinary UART state and public ABI do not grow.

Once any retained mode observes loss, it permanently latches domain_lost, preserves a previously non-SUCCESS terminal, quarantines an accepted TX, retains RX stream/FILLING duties, and attempts exactly its owned DMA stream and USART3 NVIC withdrawal.

Isolation uses actual enable-bit readback after DSB/ISB; it does not use IRQ_AVAILABLE as a runtime off proof or trust only a control-call return. Failure to prove either off enters the source-visible masked fault-observe/nonreturn loop.

DMA/mux reads and writes are guarded. Zero returned by a blocked read is not accepted as sufficient drain evidence: checked withdrawal and final mode guard must also succeed before any request/producer release.

Cache clean and pre/post invalidate occur outside the saved mask under retained loans. Reentrant observers may latch permanent loss; callback-return paths recheck before DMA programming or block publication.

TX DMA completion checks real memory EN/source facts independently of USART TC, retains the existing D2 checked TX-source withdrawal/NVIC isolation policy, and rechecks mode state after final acknowledgement immediately before clearing active and SETTLED.

RX finish checks the domain after cache work and DMA/UART acknowledgements and before publish/abort; domain loss keeps its producer loan/FILLING state even after an external restore. Prior already-published consumer loans may be released without allowing the damaged producer to restart.

Shared PIO TX uses private validation/start/cancel/prepare-settle/final-settle leaves from ordinary uart.c. RX service checks and prepares/rechecks/settles under the same saved mask, without an IRQ-restore gap or a duplicated TX state machine.

RX port stop now cancels and services any accepted shared TX through the mode-aware path before delegating to ordinary stop. If that request has not joined, stop returns BUSY instead of letting ordinary service bypass the mode fence.

Both cold initializers clear sticky state only at a fresh unowned point after ownership and hardware checks, before ordinary UART acquisition. After ordinary UART succeeds and may already have delivered an IRQ, the masked tail first claims mode responsibility and calls domain_live; an earlier observed fault cannot be erased by a tail clear.

Cold rejected/null rollback remains bounded and existing context/argument policy is preserved. No reset/gate restoration, hidden recovery, registry, extra provider worker, new public interface or new routing graph is introduced.
